name: VA-09
label: Safe R

key_factors: R+22 district partisan lean in heavily Republican southwest Virginia
Griffith's massive financial advantage ($1.8M raised vs $85K)
Incumbent seeking re-election with no polling or expert ratings suggesting vulnerability
Prediction markets price Democratic chances at about 2%
model.rationale: The district's R+22 lean, Griffith's incumbency and overwhelming fundraising edge, and markets pricing his win at 96% all point to a safe Republican hold. Joy Powers' minimal war chest gives her little capacity to compete.
model.watch: Any late polling showing the incumbent under 60% or a surge of outside Democratic spending would be the first sign of a real race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Morgan Griffith seeks another term in a southwest Virginia district that leans Republican by more than 20 points. He has raised nearly $1.8 million and holds almost $1 million on hand, while Democrat Joy Powers has raised about $85,000 with modest cash remaining. No outside groups are active against the incumbent, and no public polls or expert ratings flag the seat as competitive.

Prediction markets give Griffith roughly a 96% chance of winning, consistent with the district's fundamentals. The forecast expects a comfortable Republican victory in the range of 19 to 20 points, with the challenger needing an extraordinary shift in the political environment to make this competitive.
